returns.name: Form WH-1605, SC Withholding Quarterly Tax Return (first three quarters)
contents: Due April 30, July 31 and October 31; a return is filed for every quarter while the account is open, even with no tax or employees.
Payments alone do not satisfy the filing requirement.

returns.name: Form WH-1606, SC Withholding Fourth Quarter and Annual Reconciliation Return
contents: Due January 31 instead of a fourth-quarter WH-1605; required if the account was open for any part of the year.
W-2s and 1099s with South Carolina withholding are due by January 31: online through the W-2 portal on MyDORWAY if the IRS requires electronic W-2 filing, otherwise on paper with WH-1612.

deposits.interpretation: South Carolina requires RESIDENT employers (principal place of business in South Carolina) to pay their withholding at the same time their federal payments are due, regardless of the state amount: the federal schedule (next-day, semiweekly, monthly) applies unchanged, with no dollar bands. The due dates are the federal ones: semiweekly the Wednesday after a Wednesday-Friday payday and the Friday after a Saturday-Tuesday payday; monthly by the 15th; next-day the next business day after a payday over $100,000. NONRESIDENT employers pay quarterly or monthly instead (under $500 of South Carolina tax for the quarter: by the last day of the month after the quarter; once withholding reaches $500 in the quarter: by the 15th of the following month) and are NOT modelled here: the profile is applied as the resident rule. Payments alone do not satisfy the filing requirement. THIS IS THE 2023 EDITION of the guide.
